svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Steroid hormones act on genes."], [1, "The hormone diffuses through the plasma membrane..."], [3, "...and binds a specific intracellular receptor."], [5, "The complex enters the nucleus and binds a response element on the DNA."], [8.5, "Transcription of the target gene is switched on: mRNA is made."], [12, "The mRNA is translated: the cell makes new proteins."]]
svg.title: Steroid hormones and gene expression
svg.desc: A steroid hormone diffuses through the plasma membrane, binds an intracellular receptor, and the complex enters the nucleus and binds a response element on DNA, promoting transcription of a gene; the mRNA leaves the nucleus and is translated into protein.

g.data-info: e.g. oestradiol, progesterone or testosterone. Hydrophobic, so it diffuses straight through the plasma membrane.
A specific receptor protein in the cytoplasm (or nucleus). Binding activates it.
The hormone–receptor complex enters the nucleus and binds specific DNA sequences (response elements) near target genes.
Transcription of the target gene is promoted (or inhibited): here, mRNA is made.
The mRNA is translated at ribosomes: the cell makes different proteins. Slower than surface signalling, but longer-lasting.

g.text: slower than surface receptors, but longer-lasting effects
